title: Course order (smallest)
statement: As in Course schedule, but return an order in which to take all n courses. Many orders may be valid: return the lexicographically smallest one (always take the smallest-numbered available course). Return [] if impossible.
hints: Kahn's algorithm gives a valid order.
Choosing which available node to take next: a min-heap instead of a stack.

solution.explanation: Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap as the frontier picks the smallest available course each time, which yields the lexicographically smallest topological order (an exchange argument: taking a larger available course first can only make the sequence larger at that position). With a plain queue or stack you get some valid order in O(V + E).
solution.python:
import heapq

import heapq

def find_order(n, prereqs):
    g = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    indeg = [0] * n
    for a, b in prereqs:
        g[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    h = [i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0]
    heapq.heapify(h)
    out = []
    while h:
        u = heapq.heappop(h)
        out.append(u)
        for v in g[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                heapq.heappush(h, v)
    return out if len(out) == n else []
